items.title: Does Ka'wa'ill need his own token to pass the Aegis of the Hearth?
items.context: The Aegis is specifically designed to exclude magical creatures — and Ka'wa'ill, the merfolk companion, is one. Wilhelm (a non-covenant human) gets a token via Éogan's Arcane Connection; it's unclear whether the same trick works for, or is even offered to, Ka'wa'ill.
items.raised_event: Casting the annual Aegis of the Hearth near Harfleur
items.resolution: Answered (2026-07-25) from ArM5e core (armdef-0.4-spells-vim, Aegis of the Hearth; armdef-0.4-long-term-events, Warping). Yes — more fundamentally than Wilhelm. Ka'wa'ill is a Might creature, and RAW "No foreign supernatural creature with Might, of any type, can cross the boundary of the Aegis unless its Might exceeds the level of the Aegis." To enter he must either be made a native ("Anyone who participated in the ritual to cast the Aegis is a native of that Aegis") or be explicitly excluded ("The ritual also allows certain individuals to be excluded from the effects of the Aegis"); the covenant's token is the tracking device for that. A plain human like Wilhelm needs a token only so his own supernatural powers are not suppressed inside; Ka'wa'ill needs exclusion to cross at all. CONDITIONAL on q025: the Aegis is currently recorded at level 0 — if that is genuinely 0, any Might>0 creature already "exceeds the level" and crosses freely, making the token moot. Settle q025 to finalize.

items.title: Who is “V.,” and did they ever reach the covenant?
items.context: An unsigned letter to Solving Epicurusson, found in the GM's prep notes but never surfaced at the table or reflected in the chronicle. Addressed by courier (Mercere or trusted equivalent), it references a prior vis dispute off Saint-Valery touching the holdings of “a Tytalan recluse,” and a contact in Leuven who once gave Solving access to the Duke's private seals and warned him when Rhine Quaesitors began asking questions. The writer says their title has since been revoked and their name is now a cautionary tale in Tribunal chambers — the Rhine has become untenable, and they ask whether Solving's offer of “a covenant in motion, unanchored and burdened less by the weight of Tribunal demands” still stands. They sign only “—V.” and say they'll wait within sight of Saint Jacob's bell tower in Bruges, near the fish-market stairs, for three more cycles of the moon. Given Solving's own disappearance in Bruges in 1220, the timing may or may not be a coincidence — unclear whether this was ever meant to be picked up, or whether V. and Solving's vanishing are connected at all.
items.resolution: Already answered in verified_events.json's "Sorting through Solving's letters and documents / Finding 'V'" event: the same letter is quoted verbatim, Dagmar had Garrat Coffin investigate, a magically-tainted brooch tied to a recently-worn magus turned up, and city-guard records confirmed "the Duke's men removed someone without city sanction." The event states outright: "Rumors indicate that a man matching the description was abducted by men in the livery of the Duke of Brabant." V. never reached the covenant — likely abducted.

items.title: The Rhine Church-infiltration conspiracy Valerian uncovered is being actively investigated — outcome unknown.
items.context: Corrected framing: this did come up in play. verified_events.json's "Valerian interrogates Wilhelm about the Brabant/Church conspiracy" event confirms Valerian already knows a great deal about "a conspiracy involving the Duke of Brabant and the Church" — his follow-up questions referenced things Wilhelm hadn't yet mentioned. What remains genuinely open: what Valerian intends to do with what he knows, and whether the conspiracy itself ever gets exposed, contained, or left to fester.
items.raised_in: GM's Notion prep notes (undated), "The Situation with Valerian"
items.resolution: Canon set by GM (2026-07-25), reconciled with play-record in verified_events.json + magi.json. THE CONSPIRACY: a sect of magi from the RHINE TRIBUNAL has suborned the BISHOPRIC OF LIÈGE from within (verified_events event 60, "Valerian's Revelations") — a massive breach of the Code of Hermes (magi controlling Church hierarchy), using the Church as their proxy. It is NOT the loose "Duke of Brabant + Church" shorthand some notes use. VALERIAN: Valerian de Castellane, a Guernicus/Quaesitor of the Rhine Tribunal (magi.json), was investigating this when he was silenced and imprisoned by the Duke of Brabant — the capture happening IN BRUGES, which is politically sensitive and could provoke a response if known. The Church, acting for the Rhine magi, requested the capture; the Duke complied out of obligation to the Church and the Holy Roman Empire. Valerian had been compiling a case to bring to the GRAND TRIBUNAL. He escaped via a delayed teleportation spell hidden in the 'V' letter (nested Rego/Creo Vim), materializing on the Scholar's Wake 55 days later (events 51, 60). He is technically still a Quaesitor but "not allowed to practice"; his library is largely contraband confiscated from magi studying forbidden topics; he holds knowledge that could "ruin a lot of people's day," and traded protection to Valdemar for access to it. STILL LIVE (deliberately open): Valerian's current motivations and next move — now on the run — are unclear, to be driven by play. Whether the Liège conspiracy is ever exposed/contained is likewise open. DOWNSTREAM: this reframes c023 (the Duke's motive was obligation/coercion by Church+HRE, not merely believing forged authority) and gives t028 (Reynald, still GM-prep-only, 0 play hits) its likely role as the Rhine-trained hand inside Brabant's court. t011 (Dagmar seeing Valerian's contraband trade) is the same contraband library.

items.title: Where did Solving actually go?
items.context: The covenant's founder and Dagmar's parens vanished into Twilight from Bruges in 1220 and still hasn't returned. Old GM notes float that he may have entered the Hypostasis (the Criamon concept of escape from the cycle of time that Dagmar's own research is fixated on) — but this was never more than a GM hypothesis, and nothing in the chronicle confirms or denies it.

His return is possible but UNLIKELY — treat him as effectively gone for the foreseeable saga. The Hypostasis / Criamon 'escape from the cycle of time' framing is NOT canonized by this ruling — it remains an unconfirmed possibility (neither affirmed nor denied); promote it only if the GM later chooses to. CASCADES: q024 (with Solving effectively gone, the elder-magus tie-break vote genuinely needs settling), t052 (his envisioned vis source), t038 (sea-fae wealth bargain), and t022 (the vanish-and-return text) all hang off this.

items.title: Why was Ka'wa'ill exiled from merfolk society?
items.context: Merfolk lore in the GM's notes describes exile as "something akin to a death sentence" for most merfolk, given how insular their civilization is — which makes Ka'wa'ill's presence aboard Veðrdreki as "the merman prince" (see npcs.json) unusual and unexplained. The reason for his exile was never established.
items.resolution: Canon set by GM (2026-07-25): Ka'wa'ill's exile is really a SELF-exile driven by pride. Staying in merfolk society meant accepting a standing in the court hierarchy lower than his pride could accept, so he left rather than swallow the demotion. Fits his status as a Knight (the lowest order of the Noble caste) and his "merman prince" self-regard, and reconciles with the Exiled Atlantean flaw, which applies whether the departure was involuntary or chosen — here it was chosen.

items.title: The Duke of Brabant's relationship to the covenant, after being manipulated into imprisoning Valerian, was never resolved.

items.raised_in: GM's Notion prep notes (undated), "The Situation with Valerian"
items.resolution: Canon set by GM (2026-07-25). Duke Henry of Brabant captured Valerian (in Bruges, without city sanction; held at Breda) out of OBLIGATION to the Church and the Holy Roman Empire — the Church acting as proxy for the Rhine sect (see t027). This is the canonical motive; it supersedes the earlier prep framing of "forged authority he believed genuine" (a forged paper trail may still have existed alongside the obligation, but the driver is obligation/coercion). DEFERRED (GM: no need to determine at this time): the Duke's current beliefs about the covenant / Hermetic magi. Since Valerian self-escaped by delayed teleport rather than via a confrontation, there is no pressing aftermath to resolve — revisit only if play brings the covenant back into contact with Brabant's court.

items.title: Definitive Edition change: do Talismans still grant warping?
items.context: The GM's notes say talismans used to give warping and reportedly no longer do, but this was never confirmed as the current ruling.
items.raised_in: GM's Notion prep notes (undated), root campaign page / Foundry Notes
items.resolution: Answered (2026-07-25) from ArM5e core (armdef-0.4-long-term-events, "Warping Points and Constant Effects"): Talismans do NOT cause Warping. Verbatim: "The binding between a Hermetic magus and his familiar or Talisman does not grant Warping Points, nor do any powers enchanted into the bond." The "talismans used to give warping" memory is 4th-edition; 5e core already exempts them, so there is no Definitive-Edition change to chase.

items.title: Look up how Magic Theory is learned/created from scratch.
items.context: GM note (2026-07-14) — flagged for rules research, likely relevant to Dustin's and/or Wilhelm's teaching and folk-magic-system plans (see t019, t062).
items.resolution: Answered (2026-07-25). Two readings: (1) the Magic Theory Ability itself advances like any Arcane Ability — teaching, texts, practice (armdef-0.4-abilities). (2) Creating/integrating a whole new system into Hermetic theory is the Original Research -> Breakthrough -> Integration track, where breakthrough points convert into a new Ability or Virtue ("After the Breakthrough"). Full write-up with verbatim rules now lives at integrating_magic.html (GM Reference card on the index). Source: armdef-0.4-laboratory.

items.title: Look up how spontaneous magic integrates with the Boundary target.
items.context: GM note (2026-07-14) — flagged for rules research.
items.resolution: Answered (2026-07-25) from ArM5e core: the Boundary target forces a spell to be a Ritual (the enchantment rules note "no other reason for the spell to be a ritual, such as Year duration, Boundary target, or major effect"), and Ritual magic cannot be cast spontaneously. Therefore spontaneous magic cannot use the Boundary target at all.

Harvesting conventions vary: some sources (e.g. Fire From the Sky) require presence for a specific trigger event; others accumulate and can be harvested later, Hibernian-hedge-tradition style. (Wilhelm's 1224 Scarem Montem thesis-retrieval trip is tracked under t002/t019.)

This session's assignments: Valerian took the Kraken's Egg and the northern group handled Fire from the Sky over winter (both off-camera); Valdemar took the Diedne Garden; Dagmar took the Falcon's Cliff in spring; Dustin is collecting the Summer Fog in summer; Éogan/Owen volunteers for the Mont-Saint-Michel tide pools in fall (not a full season's activity). items.title: Tormente's errand: carry the golden crown to the estranged dragon-kin off NE England to earn passage into the Carnac regio.
items.context:
Raised session 2026-07-25 (proposed_events p052). The Carnac sea-cave regio's first threshold is guarded by TORMENTE, a magnitude-10 dragon (magic resistance in the 50s) blocking the only way deeper. Rather than fight, Dagmar parleyed a PRICE: Tormente handed him a heavy jewelled golden crown (Roman in style) to carry as an OFFERING OF PEACE to its estranged kin — another dragon that 'will not speak to me,' dwelling in a sea-cliff cave ABOVE the waves off the English northeast coast, near Scarborough / Newcastle, just short of Scotland. Reconcile the two, and Tormente will deem Dagmar worthy of passing deeper into the regio. Dagmar accepted and gave orders to sail NORTH — probably via Stonehenge to collect Llewellyn and finally cash in the time-crystal en route (see t018). OPEN QUESTIONS TO DEVELOP: (a) the kin's disposition — why the estrangement, and whether a crown actually mends it or the kin is hostile; (b) 'Jeffrey the First' — Tormente asked whether Dagmar served this long-dead king of Brittany, whose 'quest of learning' it seems to guard; who he was and why the regio's guardian tests seekers in his name is unexplained; (c) the wrinkle that Foxglove robbed Tormente's hoard the same night (c026), which could sour the goodwill this errand depends on. This is Dagmar's active quest; t025 (the regio proper) stays gated behind it.

DEVELOPED (session prep 2026-08-08, q027 #4): the 'estranged kin' is MÍMORMR, a cursed bone-speaking scholar-wyrm off the NE English coast (full detail in the new t072). The errand is not what it looks like: Tormente is a TRICKSTER, the Roman crown is the KEY that BREAKS a curse Tormente itself laid, and carrying it 'in peace' actually UNBINDS Mímormr — who becomes a regional environmental threat once loose. Dagmar is an unwitting cat's-paw; completing the errand earns passage into the regio (t025) at the region's expense. Mímormr's false-but-sincere claim to descend from Jörmungandr, and the NE-England worm-legend tie, are in t072.
items.raised_event: Into the Carnac regio: the dragon Tormente
items.resolution: Resolved (2026-08-08): Dagmar carried the crown north and delivered it to the estranged kin — the worm Mímormr, in a cliff-cave NE of York. The crown was a name-release, not a gift: it FREED Mímormr, whom Tormente had bound. Mímormr gave Dagmar a token to return to Tormente as proof. Regio passage is now owed by Tormente; the fallout (a loosed wyrm) is tracked in c027, and the return to Tormente in t073.

items.title: Who name-bound Mímormr, in a magic that isn't Hermetic?
items.context: Examining the empty cave, the magi found the binding was NOT Hermetic: a Muto-Terram-scale warping of the stone against its grain, plus an Adamic (True Name) binding of Mímormr's body to the location — power that would tax a trained Hermetic magus to match. Who worked it, in what tradition, and how it relates to Tormente is unknown.
items.resolution: Resolved (2026-08-19): it was TORMENTE. The non-Hermetic working that sealed Mímormr — the against-the-grain Muto-Terram warping of the stone plus the Adamic (True Name) binding of Mímormr's body to the cave — was Tormente's own hand, not a rival tradition's. This recasts the crown-errand (t066) and the jailbreak Tormente set Dagmar (t072/t073): the trickster wyrm bound Mímormr itself, and is now steering the covenant into undoing that binding.

items.title: What are we preparing for next session?
items.context:
As of the end of Spring 1224 the party is split across two threads — Wilhelm & Éogan making their way home from Ireland, and Dagmar running north from the half-opened Carnac regio (proposed_events p047–p054). This is the GM's working slate of candidate scenes to develop and stage for the next session. The answers so far:

1) WHAT DO WILHELM'S ASSISTANTS BRING BACK — AND COULD IT NEGATE THE HYPOTHESIS? Wilhelm's research assistants were sent west and south over the winter (p049), paid in grain and silver, to gather hedge-tradition material. The beat is what they return with at the rendezvous — and specifically whether any of it FALSIFIES the folk-magic thesis rather than confirming it: a tradition that works WITHOUT leaning on the environment (the inverse of the Uisneach augury insight, p047), or the open-ocean storm-prediction / current-finding citation the thesis still lacks (t009) turning out not to exist, or to cut against the 'context and time-of-year matter' core (t019). A negative result forces Wilhelm to revise before he can deliver to Scarem Montem (see #6). Cross-ref t009, t019. [DEVELOPED 2026-08-08: the negation is a MADNESS failure rate that breaks the scalable/vis-factory case without disproving the magic (t019, t020, q028); the assistants also flag a temporal hedge mage who beat the Limit of Time, leaving Wilhelm an origin-less brass acorn (t071).]

2) WHERE DOES FOXGLOVE GET OFF THE SHIP? Foxglove is aboard carrying roughly five bags of stolen Roman dragon-gold (c026), lifted the same night Dagmar agreed to run Tormente's peace-errand (t066). She has every reason to disembark and vanish with the hoard before the theft surfaces — and the Tide of Memory is already running north up the English coast toward a Stonehenge-Tribunal port (p054), an obvious jumping-off point. Settle at which port she gets off (and whether she deserts outright), and what the fallout is if she is still aboard when Dagmar returns to Tormente and the missing hoard is noticed. Cross-ref c026, t066. [DEVELOPED 2026-08-08: these are player calls; what got prepped is the WORLD constraint — a GM reference on converting Roman gold c.1224 (no gold coinage / silver standard, so bullion-by-weight only; melt, goldsmiths, Jewish moneylenders, Flanders/Lombard bankers, worked goods, the Church; treasure-trove and provenance friction; no collector market yet) now lives in c026.]

3) DOES VALDEMAR JOIN DAGMAR FOR THE DRAGON LEG? The northbound errand — carry the jewelled crown to Tormente's estranged kin off Scarborough / Newcastle (t066) — is a two-magus job waiting to happen. Dagmar has already invited Llewellyn ex Miscellanea by Redcap (p054); Valdemar Bjornsson, a PC magus with no familiar yet (t037) and an established tie to the sea-fae Rán (c022), is a natural companion for dragon diplomacy. Decide whether Valdemar signs on, what he brings, and how his Rán connection reads to a dragon claiming Norse descent (see #4). Cross-ref t066, t037, c022. [DEFERRED 2026-08-08: Valdemar's player has been absent; GM to improvise whether he joins rather than prep it in advance.]

4) THE KIN-DRAGON CLAIMS TO BE A CHILD OF JÖRMUNGANDR. The reveal waiting behind t066(b): the estranged dragon off the English northeast coast (or Tormente itself) claims descent from Jörmungandr, the Midgard Serpent — styling itself the greatest magical being that ever was. For a Norse-seiðr saga this is a major cosmological escalation — it recontextualizes the Carnac regio's guardianship, the unexplained 'Jeffrey the First / quest of learning' hook, and frames Tormente's magnitude-10 Might as merely the lesser sibling's. Decide how literally true the claim is, what Might / scale it implies, and how it lands against the saga's existing Norse threads (Rán, the sea-fae). Cross-ref t066. [DEVELOPED 2026-08-08: the claim is FALSE but sincerely believed by MÍMORMR, a cursed bone-speaking scholar-wyrm; Tormente (a trickster) is using Dagmar to break its curse, and freeing it looses a regional threat — full build in the new t072.]

5) ÉOGAN AND THE CAPRICORN. Already logged as GM intent (t070): on the sea voyage home from Ireland a Magic-realm capricorn (sea-goat) singles Éogan out and paces his ship — the 'small fae drawn to Éogan/Stijntje' thread (t068) escalated to a Might-bearing creature and offered as his first familiar prospect (t037). The work is courting it and the binding lab-work, not an instant bond. Placement: the Spring/Summer 1224 voyage home. Cross-ref t070, t068, t037. [DEVELOPED 2026-08-08: draw is independent of the t068 fae affinity; signature specialty is CROSSING THRESHOLDS INTO REGIONES; mythological grounding (Enki's Goat-Fish / Macrobius's Gate of the Gods), corpus build/bind references, and a suggested Might ~12–16 Magic build all recorded in t070. What it wants in exchange remains open.]

6) DOES WILHELM SAIL TO SCAREM MONTEM? The ship-for-book swap is confirmed in motion — the Hound of Cassel is under Wilhelm's control and headed back to Scarem Montem (t002, Resolved) — and what he owes them is the folk-magic thesis. The delivery scene therefore hinges on #1: whether the assistants' material firms up (or breaks) the thesis's weakest citation (t009) decides whether Wilhelm arrives with a finished thesis or one still short a maritime example. Cross-ref t002, t009. [DEVELOPED 2026-08-08: the three sealed chests aboard the Hound of Cassel (c012) are now defined — intercepted Bishopric-of-Liège↔Scarem Montem cipher letters exposing a Church/State suborning (Code violation, tied to the Brabant conspiracy t028/c023/t027). Ring-based public/private-key crypto means the covenant can PROVE the correspondents but mostly can't read the content. Wilhelm may be carrying Scarem Montem's own incriminating mail back to them — return, keep, or weaponise it in the swap?]

Update (2026-08-10) — refocused for the 22nd (into Fall 1224). With #2/#3/#4 and the Rody hand-off now PLAYED (see the Chronicle), the next-session slate narrows to three spines: (A) Wilhelm's delivery run to Scarem Montem — the thesis gate #1 (s1) feeding the delivery #6 (s6); (B) Dagmar's push into the regiones gated behind Tormente — the return with Mímormr's token (s8), Llewellyn's time-flow gambit (s9), and the wider regio cluster (s10); and (C) a NEW home-front spine — Confluensis turning the screws (s11, t078), the soured-liege reprisal (c019/c022) finally going active while the magi are scattered. Éogan's capricorn (#5/s5) rides along on the voyage home.

items.title: Was Solving the Diedne who planted the Garden?
items.context:
CONFLICT IN THE RECORD. The Spring 1224 verified event 'Valdemar harvests the Diedne Garden' states he means to look closer at the ruined Diedne site, 'curious whether the vanished founder SOLVING left anything there unseen.' The next-session prep (s12) instead speaks of a long-dead Diedne planter. These are not the same claim and the difference is large.

IF SOLVING PLANTED IT: Sjórseiðr's own vanished founder was House Diedne. Valdemar is then not the only one, his 'personal draw' to the garden is inheritance rather than coincidence, and Solving's disappearance — and the whole 'finding V' correspondence arc — reads differently. It would also mean the covenant has been holding a Diedne lineage since its founding, which changes what a Confluensis complaint could turn up (t078).

IF NOT: the planter is an unnamed pre-Schism Diedne, Solving's interest was scholarly or opportunistic, and Valdemar's draw stays personal and private.

Needs a GM ruling before s12 is staged, because the initiation ladder in t082 reads completely differently depending on whose circle he is standing in.

LINKS: t082, t078, s12.
items.resolution: Resolved (2026-08-22): Solving did NOT plant the garden and is NOT House Diedne. The planter is an unnamed pre-Schism Diedne; Solving's interest (per the Spring 1224 'Valdemar harvests the Diedne Garden' event) was scholarly/opportunistic at most. Valdemar's draw to the garden stays personal and private — not inheritance. The 'IF SOLVING PLANTED IT' branch is closed; s12's 'long-dead planter' framing stands.
